[Loka+ṇa]  CL=7 (1) Types of Loka (Worlds) about Beings (A) The Human World (Loka). (B) The World of Swans (Hamsa Loka) (Rare term, may refer to a mythical or symbolic realm). (C) The World of Grammar Scholars (Referring to those engaged in linguistic studies. (D) The World of Fools (Bāla Loka). (E) The Human World (Loka of Humans). (F) The Rūpāvacara Brahma Realm (Form Brahma World). (G) The Realms of Devas, Humans, and Brahmas (Referring to the happy existences in Saṃsāra).(H) The World of Sensual Beings (Kāma-Puggala-Satta Loka) (Beings existing in the Sensual Realms). (I) The Hell Realm (World of Hell Beings) (Referring to beings suffering in hellish existences). (2) Types of Loka (Worlds) about Places. (A) The Spatial World (Ākāsa Loka / Universe). (B) The Hell Realm (Naraka Loka). (C) The Animal Realm (Tiracchāna Loka). (D) The Human World (Loka of Humans) (Repeated for emphasis). (E) The Infinite Universe (The Undivided World/Limitless Cosmos) (Referring to the vast, boundless universe). (3) Types of Loka (Worlds) in Relation to Dhamma. (A) The World of Conditioned Phenomena (Saṅkhāra Loka) (Referring to all compounded things). (B) The World of the Noble Truth of Suffering (Dukkha Sacca Loka) (Referring to the reality of suffering as a world in itself. (C) The World of the Five Aggregates (Khandha Loka) (Referring to existence as defined by the aggregates: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness). (D) The World of Others’ Forms, Feelings, and Phenomena (Referring to external physical and mental phenomena perceived by individuals).  (E) Five aggregates of an individual such as one’s form and suffering. (F) Five aggregates of other individuals such as his/her form and suffering. (G) Twelve aspects of sense bases (Āyatanā). (H) Eighteen aspects of dhatu. (I) The eighteen aspects of dhatu in the lower realm. (J) The resultant existence in a bad destination.
(K) Kamma-process becoming in a bad destination. (L) The resultant existence in a good destination. (M) Kamma-process becoming in a good destination. (N) The volitional transformation phenomena that is designated as “living being.”(O) The realm of form and consciousness. (P) Three aspects of suffering. (Q) The realm of nutriment (Āhāraloka). (R) The realm of the pile of fuel (Upādānakkhandhāloka), five aggregates that are the sense base of upādāna. (S) Six aspects of internal sense organs. (T) Six aspects of Apaāyatana. (U) The seven bases of the paṭisandhi viññāṇa. (V) Eight aspects of worldly matter (lokadhamma). (W) Nine places of living beings. (X) The ten aspects of the form of sense base. (Y) Five aspects of pasādarūpa. (Z) Five aspects of the object of sensual pleasure. (AA) The body or the realm of form. (BB) The mental realm. (CC) The obstacle phenomena (nīvaraṇa dhamma). (DD) Khandhā, āyatana, dhatu. (EE) The present world.
